history.summary: One of the oldest Shiva temples of Muzaffarpur, known as the 'Deoghar of Bihar'; the presiding deity is Garibnath ('Lord of the poor'). Belief: a dense forest with seven peepal trees stood here; when the trees were cut, a blood-red substance appeared and a huge lingam was found, after which Baba appeared in the landowner's dream - worship began. Wikipedia credits creator Mahavir Chachan and lists Nagara architecture; governed by the Bihar State Board of Religious Trusts. Some tourism sites claim Mahabharata-era origins, which conflicts with the documented ~300-year history (flagged as legend). name: Baba Garib Nath Temple
town_description: Muzaffarpur is a major city in North Bihar and the commercial capital of the Tirhut region, famous worldwide for its Shahi litchi. It is a large railway junction about 70 km north of Patna.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (about 70 km)
travel.road: In the heart of the city on Garib Asthan Road (Reva Road), near Chhata Bazaar/Makhan Sah Chowk; easily reached by city road

visitor_information.best_time: Shravan month (July-August) and Maha Shivaratri, when the temple is most crowded and decorated
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: travelsetu.com lists 5:00 AM-10:00 PM daily; templedarshan.live lists 4:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:00 PM (verify before visiting)
